title: Eisenstein and colleagues, 2005: a correlation peak at 100 h^−1 Mpc
summary: From 46,748 luminous red galaxies, the SDSS correlation function shows a peak at 100 h^−1 Mpc, which the authors identify with the predicted baryon acoustic scale.
body: The abstract of Eisenstein and colleagues reports the correlation function of 46,748 luminous red galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, over 3,816 square degrees and 0.16 < z < 0.47, a volume of 0.72 h^−3 Gpc^3. It says there is a detected peak at 100 h^−1 Mpc that matches the predicted shape and location of the recombination-era acoustic oscillations. The peak detection is a measurement of the galaxy correlation function. The identification of that peak with the sound horizon, and the statement that it demonstrates linear growth since z = 1000, are the authors' interpretation of the peak. The abstract says the acoustic peak measures the ratio of distances to z = 0.35 and z = 1089 to 4 percent fractional accuracy, and the absolute distance to z = 0.35 to 5 percent.

sources.title: Detection of the Baryon Acoustic Peak in the Large-Scale Correlation Function of SDSS Luminous Red Galaxies
sources.author: D. J. Eisenstein and colleagues
